verdict.rationale: A changelog entry shows a PostgreSQL branch can be created restored to a point-in-time timestamp via --restore-point, and the Postgres docs say branches can be restored from backups. For Vitess, the evidence only shows daily scheduled backups, manual backups and backup restore, not arbitrary point-in-time recovery. Missing for 10: documented PITR retention window and granularity, point-in-time recovery for Vitess databases, in-depth first-party PITR docs beyond a changelog line, independent or hands-on corroboration of recovery from bad writes.
